_comment: H2 (docs/design/1.6.0-TRACKER.md): 'conformance rigs carry one cell per Teller step per plane'.
Steps are ARCHITECTURE.md #2.2 (arrival, decode, authenticate, verify, approve, admit, route,
meter, audit, exit). This is the plane x step MATRIX: for every cell, either an id that names a
real, run scenario in one of the conformance rigs (or the shadow oracle, for the llm plane), or
the literal string "none" naming a genuine gap. 'gating' marks the 7 steps whose contract H2
spells out explicitly (a refusal/outcome that must never leak past its step); the other 3
(arrival, decode, approve) are mapped for completeness but do not fail the --check by themselves
when a shared, plane-agnostic kernel cell already covers them for every plane at once.
Checked by: scripts/teller-steps-check.py --check. Wired into scripts/verify-1.6.0-done.sh
beside the ISOMORPHISM group.
THE ROOT COLUMN (`root_legs` + every cell's `root`). The `cell` above is the SHIPPED path: the
step proven where a conformance rig drives the plane as an operator would. All five planes now
also run through the composition root, behind root-llm / root-mcp / root-a2a / root-voice /
root-admin, and a step proven on the rig and unwitnessed over the loop is the same half-answer.
So every cell carries a SECOND verdict over its plane's root leg:
proven -- with `test`: a `<crates/busbar/src/root/units_*.rs>::<test fn>` cell that drives the
step through run_unit. The check verifies the file is the leg's own and the fn is in
it; `--root-legs` EXECUTES every one of them with all five features on.
none   -- with `note`: what the leg does instead, and why no cell drives this step yet. R-16:
name a gap, never paper it.
The root column's gaps are PRINTED and named on every run but do not fail --check by themselves.
The legs are default-OFF and are being switched over plane by plane, so the shipped path is what
the gating rule is about; the root gaps are the switch-over queue. What IS red on this column: a
`proven` root cell whose named test does not exist, and a leg with no proven cell at all.
The two columns are independent verdicts about the same step and either may be "none" alone:
mcp.approve and a2a.decode are exactly that shape today -- open on the rig, proven over the loop.
